claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're caring for.

**Could you please tell me the name and date of birth of the child or children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 12 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 12 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and if so, what is your residency status (for example, are you a British citizen, EU citizen, or do you have settled/pre-settled status)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Now I need to understand your living arrangements and who Alex lives with.

**Does Alex live with you in Manchester full-time, or does Alex spend time with another parent or carer?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me full-time here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that. That's useful to know.

Now I need to check on your work and income situation, as this can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

**Are you currently working, and if so, what is your approximate annual income (or your partner's income if you have one)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working, yes. Why do you need to know about my income? I thought Child Benefit was available to everyone regardless of income?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a very good question, and I appreciate you asking! You're right that Child Benefit is generally available regardless of your income level. However, there is a High Income Child Benefit Charge that applies if your income (or your partner's income) exceeds a certain threshold, which can affect the benefit you receive.

Additionally, I need to understand your full circumstances to ensure there are no other factors that might affect eligibility.

**Could you tell me what your approximate annual income is? This will help me give you an accurate assessment.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. Well, I earn around £45,000 a year, and I don't have a partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful.

I just need to confirm one more thing to complete my assessment.

**Is Alex a British citizen, or does Alex have a different immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen like me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review your circumstances:

- You are a British citizen living in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is your child, 12 years old, and a British citizen
- Alex lives with you full-time
- Your annual income is approximately £45,000

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you meet all the key requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Your income of £45,000 is below the High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold (which begins to apply at £50,000), so you would receive the full Child Benefit entitlement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

To summarise why:
- Alex is a British citizen and under 16 years old
- You are a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- Alex lives with you full-time
- Your income is below the threshold where the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply

You should be able to claim the full Child Benefit entitlement for Alex. If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim through the UK government's official Child Benefit application process.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
